It solves the problem of efficiently filtering out inactive or merged Gaussians without allocating separate boolean flags or requiring complex metadata lookups [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that to detect a disabled (inactive) splat, the system reads specific words from the Uint32Arrays and checks for specific bit patterns (0xfc00). It further states that if a splat is disabled, its coordinates are set to NaN to exclude it from queries. This mechanism avoids the need for separate boolean flags or complex metadata lookups, as the status is embedded directly in the data structure's existing fields via specific bit patterns. Thus, the claim that it solves the problem of efficiently filtering out inactive/merged Gaussians without allocating separate boolean flags or requiring complex metadata lookups is supported by the evidence.
